text.p: - Supreme commander of NATO Europe George A. Joulwan started a two-day visit to Slovenia on Wednesday. He will discuss Slovenian cooperation in the Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Bosnia and ways for Slovenia to join NATO.
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek on Wednesday visited his Norwegian counterpart Thorbjoern Jagland and discussed bilateral cooperation and Slovenian entry to NATO.

- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler on Wednesday visited his Austrian counterpart Wolfgang Schuessel to discuss relations between the neighbouring countries and the possible entry of both countries to NATO in future.
- Slovenia won the first point in soccer World Cup qualifications after drawing 3-3 against favoured Croatia in Split on Wednesday.

- Slovenia is subsidising its public health system with an average of 900 marks ($537.9) per citizen annually, compared to the EU average of between 2,500 and 3,000 marks per citizen, Primoz Rode, general director of Ljubljana's Clinical centre said.
- A delegation of the German parliament economic board visited the Slovenian parliament on Wednesday.
- Slovenian and Croatian transport ministers on Wednesday signed an agreement on railway traffic in border areas.
- The number of pensioners in Slovenia, which has a population of two million, increased to 265,341 from 111,975 over the past 15 years, the country's pensioners fund said.
- About 270 exhibitors from 16 countries are taking part in the 36th cooking fair that started in Ljubljana on Wednesday. REUTER
